audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Exodus / Shemot golden calf rupture text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for golden calf, Aaron, covenant rupture, Moses intercession, broken tablets, Levite violence, and plague. Strong anti-idolatry and anti-violence safeguards required.

verses.restored: The people saw that Moses delayed to come down from the mountain, and the people gathered against Aaron and said to him, Rise, make for us gods who will go before us, for this Moses, the man who brought us up from land of Egypt, we do not know what has become of him.

familiar.text: And when the people saw that Moses delayed to come down out of the mount, the people gathered themselves together unto Aaron, and said unto him, Up, make us gods, which shall go before us; for as for this Moses, the man that brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we wot not what is become of him.

modern.text: Now when the people saw that Moses was delayed in coming down from the mountain, they gathered around Aaron and said, “Come, make us gods who will go before us. As for this Moses who brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him!”

original.text: וַיַּ֣רְא הָעָ֔ם כִּֽי בֹשֵׁ֥שׁ מֹשֶׁ֖ה לָרֶ֣דֶת מִן הָהָ֑ר וַיִּקָּהֵ֨ל הָעָ֜ם עַֽל אַהֲרֹ֗ן וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ אֵלָיו֙ ק֣וּם עֲשֵׂה לָ֣נוּ אֱלֹהִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר יֵֽלְכוּ֙ לְפָנֵ֔ינוּ כִּי זֶ֣ה מֹשֶׁ֣ה הָאִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֤ר הֶֽעֱלָ֨נוּ֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם לֹ֥א יָדַ֖עְנוּ מֶה הָ֥יָה לֽוֹ

verses.restored: Aaron said to them, Tear off gold rings that are in ears of your wives, sons, and daughters, and bring them to me.

familiar.text: And Aaron said unto them, Break off the golden earrings, which are in the ears of your wives, of your sons, and of your daughters, and bring them unto me.

modern.text: So Aaron told them, “Take off the gold earrings that are on your wives and sons and daughters, and bring them to me.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ אַהֲרֹ֔ן פָּֽרְקוּ֙ נִזְמֵ֣י הַזָּהָ֔ב אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּאָזְנֵ֣י נְשֵׁיכֶ֔ם בְּנֵיכֶ֖ם וּבְנֹתֵיכֶ֑ם וְהָבִ֖יאוּ אֵלָֽי

verses.restored: All the people tore off gold rings that were in their ears and brought them to Aaron.

familiar.text: And all the people brake off the golden earrings which were in their ears, and brought them unto Aaron.

modern.text: Then all the people took off their gold earrings and brought them to Aaron.

original.text: וַיִּתְפָּֽרְקוּ֙ כָּל הָעָ֔ם אֶת נִזְמֵ֥י הַזָּהָ֖ב אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּאָזְנֵיהֶ֑ם וַיָּבִ֖יאוּ אֶֽל אַהֲרֹֽן

verses.restored: He took from their hand, fashioned it with engraving tool, and made it a molten calf. They said, These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from land of Egypt.

familiar.text: And he received them at their hand, and fashioned it with a graving tool, after he had made it a molten calf: and they said, These be thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.

modern.text: He took the gold from their hands, and with an engraving tool he fashioned it into a molten calf. And they said, “These, O Israel, are your gods, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt!”

original.text: וַיִּקַּ֣ח מִיָּדָ֗ם וַיָּ֤צַר אֹתוֹ֙ בַּחֶ֔רֶט וַֽיַּעֲשֵׂ֖הוּ עֵ֣גֶל מַסֵּכָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ אֵ֤לֶּה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶעֱל֖וּךָ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם

verses.restored: Aaron saw, and built altar before it; Aaron called out and said, Festival to YHWH tomorrow.

familiar.text: And when Aaron saw it, he built an altar before it; and Aaron made proclamation, and said, To morrow is a feast to the LORD.

modern.text: When Aaron saw this, he built an altar before the calf and proclaimed: “Tomorrow shall be a feast to the LORD.”

original.text: וַיַּ֣רְא אַהֲרֹ֔ן וַיִּ֥בֶן מִזְבֵּ֖חַ לְפָנָ֑יו וַיִּקְרָ֤א אַֽהֲרֹן֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר חַ֥ג לַיהוָ֖ה מָחָֽר

verses.restored: They rose early next day, offered burnt offerings and brought near peace offerings; the people sat to eat and drink, and rose to play.

familiar.text: And they rose up early on the morrow, and offered burnt offerings, and brought peace offerings; and the people sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play.

modern.text: So the next day they arose, offered burnt offerings, and presented peace offerings. And the people sat down to eat and drink, and got up to indulge in revelry.

original.text: וַיַּשְׁכִּ֨ימוּ֙ מִֽמָּחֳרָ֔ת וַיַּעֲל֣וּ עֹלֹ֔ת וַיַּגִּ֖שׁוּ שְׁלָמִ֑ים וַיֵּ֤שֶׁב הָעָם֙ לֶֽאֱכֹ֣ל וְשָׁת֔וֹ וַיָּקֻ֖מוּ לְצַחֵֽק

verses.restored: YHWH spoke to Moses, Go, descend, for your people whom you brought up from land of Egypt have corrupted themselves.

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto Moses, Go, get thee down; for thy people, which thou broughtest out of the land of Egypt, have corrupted themselves:

modern.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go down at once, for your people, whom you brought up out of the land of Egypt, have corrupted themselves.

original.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל מֹשֶׁ֑ה לֶךְ רֵ֕ד כִּ֚י שִׁחֵ֣ת עַמְּךָ֔ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶעֱלֵ֖יתָ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם

verses.restored: They turned aside quickly from way I commanded them; they made for themselves a molten calf, bowed to it, sacrificed to it, and said, These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from land of Egypt.

familiar.text: They have turned aside quickly out of the way which I commanded them: they have made them a molten calf, and have worshipped it, and have sacrificed thereunto, and said, These be thy gods, O Israel, which have brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.

modern.text: How quickly they have turned aside from the way that I commanded them! They have made for themselves a molten calf and have bowed down to it. They have sacrificed to it and said, ‘These, O Israel, are your gods, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt.’”

original.text: סָ֣רוּ מַהֵ֗ר מִן הַדֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּיתִ֔ם עָשׂ֣וּ לָהֶ֔ם עֵ֖גֶל מַסֵּכָ֑ה וַיִּשְׁתַּֽחֲווּ לוֹ֙ וַיִּזְבְּחוּ ל֔וֹ וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ אֵ֤לֶּה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶֽעֱל֖וּךָ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם

verses.restored: YHWH said to Moses, I have seen this people, and look, it is a stiff-necked people.

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto Moses, I have seen this people, and, behold, it is a stiffnecked people:

modern.text: The LORD also said to Moses, “I have seen this people, and they are indeed a stiff-necked people.

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל מֹשֶׁ֑ה רָאִ֨יתִי֙ אֶת הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה עַם קְשֵׁה עֹ֖רֶף הֽוּא

verses.restored: Now leave me alone, so my anger may burn against them and consume them, and I will make you into a great nation.

familiar.text: Now therefore let me alone, that my wrath may wax hot against them, and that I may consume them: and I will make of thee a great nation.

modern.text: Now leave Me alone, so that My anger may burn against them and consume them. Then I will make you into a great nation.”

original.text: וְעַתָּה֙ הַנִּ֣יחָה לִּ֔י וְיִֽחַר אַפִּ֥י בָהֶ֖ם וַאֲכַלֵּ֑ם וְאֶֽעֱשֶׂ֥ה אוֹתְךָ֖ לְג֥וֹי גָּדֽוֹל

verses.restored: Moses entreated face of YHWH his Divine and said, YHWH, why should your anger burn against your people whom you brought out from land of Egypt with great power and strong hand?

familiar.text: And Moses besought the LORD his God, and said, LORD, why doth thy wrath wax hot against thy people, which thou hast brought forth out of the land of Egypt with great power, and with a mighty hand?

modern.text: But Moses sought the favor of the LORD his God, saying, “O LORD, why does Your anger burn against Your people, whom You brought out of the land of Egypt with great power and a mighty hand?

original.text: וַיְחַ֣ל מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֶת פְּנֵ֖י יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑יו וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לָמָ֤ה יְהוָה֙ יֶחֱרֶ֤ה אַפְּךָ֙ בְּעַמֶּ֔ךָ אֲשֶׁ֤ר הוֹצֵ֨אתָ֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם בְּכֹ֥חַ גָּד֖וֹל וּבְיָ֥ד חֲזָקָֽה

verses.restored: Why should Egypt say, With evil he brought them out, to kill them in mountains and consume them from face of ground? Turn from burning anger and relent concerning harm to your people.

familiar.text: Wherefore should the Egyptians speak, and say, For mischief did he bring them out, to slay them in the mountains, and to consume them from the face of the earth? Turn from thy fierce wrath, and repent of this evil against thy people.

modern.text: Why should the Egyptians declare, ‘He brought them out with evil intent, to kill them in the mountains and wipe them from the face of the earth’? Turn from Your fierce anger and relent from doing harm to Your people.

original.text: לָמָּה֩ יֹאמְר֨וּ מִצְרַ֜יִם לֵאמֹ֗ר בְּרָעָ֤ה הֽוֹצִיאָם֙ לַהֲרֹ֤ג אֹתָם֙ בֶּֽהָרִ֔ים וּ֨לְכַלֹּתָ֔ם מֵעַ֖ל פְּנֵ֣י הָֽאֲדָמָ֑ה שׁ֚וּב מֵחֲר֣וֹן אַפֶּ֔ךָ וְהִנָּחֵ֥ם עַל הָרָעָ֖ה לְעַמֶּֽךָ

verses.restored: Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, your servants, to whom you swore by yourself and spoke to them: I will multiply your seed like stars of heavens, and all this land I said I will give to your seed, and they shall inherit into the age.

familiar.text: Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, thy servants, to whom thou swarest by thine own self, and saidst unto them, I will multiply your seed as the stars of heaven, and all this land that I have spoken of will I give unto your seed, and they shall inherit it for ever.

modern.text: Remember Your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, to whom You swore by Your very self when You declared, ‘I will make your descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky, and I will give your descendants all this land that I have promised, and it shall be their inheritance forever.’”

original.text: זְכֹ֡ר לְאַבְרָהָם֩ לְיִצְחָ֨ק וּלְיִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל עֲבָדֶ֗יךָ אֲשֶׁ֨ר נִשְׁבַּ֣עְתָּ לָהֶם֮ בָּךְ֒ וַתְּדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם אַרְבֶּה֙ אֶֽת זַרְעֲכֶ֔ם כְּכוֹכְבֵ֖י הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וְכָל הָאָ֨רֶץ הַזֹּ֜את אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמַ֗רְתִּי אֶתֵּן֙ לְזַרְעֲכֶ֔ם וְנָחֲל֖וּ לְעֹלָֽם

verses.restored: YHWH relented concerning harm that he spoke to do to his people.

familiar.text: And the LORD repented of the evil which he thought to do unto his people.

modern.text: So the LORD relented from the calamity He had threatened to bring on His people.

original.text: וַיִּנָּ֖חֶם יְהוָ֑ה עַל הָ֣רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֶּ֖ר לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת לְעַמּֽוֹ

verses.restored: Moses turned and descended from mountain, with two tablets of testimony in his hand, tablets written on both sides, from this and from that they were written.

familiar.text: And Moses turned, and went down from the mount, and the two tables of the testimony were in his hand: the tables were written on both their sides; on the one side and on the other were they written.

modern.text: Then Moses turned and went down the mountain with the two tablets of the Testimony in his hands. They were inscribed on both sides, front and back.

original.text: וַיִּ֜פֶן וַיֵּ֤רֶד מֹשֶׁה֙ מִן הָהָ֔ר וּשְׁנֵ֛י לֻחֹ֥ת הָעֵדֻ֖ת בְּיָד֑וֹ לֻחֹ֗ת כְּתֻבִים֙ מִשְּׁנֵ֣י עֶבְרֵיהֶ֔ם מִזֶּ֥ה וּמִזֶּ֖ה הֵ֥ם כְּתֻבִֽים

verses.restored: The tablets were work of Divine, and writing was writing of Divine, engraved upon tablets.

familiar.text: And the tables were the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God, graven upon the tables.

modern.text: The tablets were the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God, engraved on the tablets.

original.text: וְהַ֨לֻּחֹ֔ת מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים הֵ֑מָּה וְהַמִּכְתָּ֗ב מִכְתַּ֤ב אֱלֹהִים֙ ה֔וּא חָר֖וּת עַל הַלֻּחֹֽת

verses.restored: Joshua heard voice of people in its noise and said to Moses, Sound of war is in camp.

familiar.text: And when Joshua heard the noise of the people as they shouted, he said unto Moses, There is a noise of war in the camp.

modern.text: When Joshua heard the sound of the people shouting, he said to Moses, “The sound of war is in the camp.”

original.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֧ע יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ אֶת ק֥וֹל הָעָ֖ם בְּרֵעֹ֑ה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל מֹשֶׁ֔ה ק֥וֹל מִלְחָמָ֖ה בַּֽמַּחֲנֶה

verses.restored: He said, It is not sound of answering strength, nor sound of answering weakness; sound of singing I hear.

familiar.text: And he said, It is not the voice of them that shout for mastery, neither is it the voice of them that cry for being overcome: but the noise of them that sing do I hear.

modern.text: But Moses replied: “It is neither the cry of victory nor the cry of defeat; I hear the sound of singing!”

original.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אֵ֥ין קוֹל֙ עֲנ֣וֹת גְּבוּרָ֔ה וְאֵ֥ין ק֖וֹל עֲנ֣וֹת חֲלוּשָׁ֑ה ק֣וֹל עַנּ֔וֹת אָנֹכִ֖י שֹׁמֵֽעַ

verses.restored: It happened as he came near camp and saw calf and dances, Moses' anger burned; he threw tablets from his hands and shattered them under mountain.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, as soon as he came nigh unto the camp, that he saw the calf, and the dancing: and Moses’ anger waxed hot, and he cast the tables out of his hands, and brake them beneath the mount.

modern.text: As Moses approached the camp and saw the calf and the dancing, he burned with anger and threw the tablets out of his hands, shattering them at the base of the mountain.

original.text: וַֽיְהִ֗י כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר קָרַב֙ אֶל הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וַיַּ֥רְא אֶת הָעֵ֖גֶל וּמְחֹלֹ֑ת וַיִּֽחַר אַ֣ף מֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיַּשְׁלֵ֤ךְ מידו אֶת הַלֻּחֹ֔ת וַיְשַׁבֵּ֥ר אֹתָ֖ם תַּ֥חַת הָהָֽר

verses.restored: He took calf they had made, burned it with fire, ground it until fine, scattered upon face of waters, and made children of Israel drink.

familiar.text: And he took the calf which they had made, and burnt it in the fire, and ground it to powder, and strawed it upon the water, and made the children of Israel drink of it.

modern.text: Then he took the calf they had made, burned it in the fire, ground it to powder, and scattered the powder over the face of the water. Then he forced the Israelites to drink it.

original.text: וַיִּקַּ֞ח אֶת הָעֵ֨גֶל אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשׂוּ֙ וַיִּשְׂרֹ֣ף בָּאֵ֔שׁ וַיִּטְחַ֖ן עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁר דָּ֑ק וַיִּ֨זֶר֙ עַל פְּנֵ֣י הַמַּ֔יִם וַיַּ֖שְׁקְ אֶת בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: Moses said to Aaron, What did this people do to you, that you brought upon them great sin/misalignment?

familiar.text: And Moses said unto Aaron, What did this people unto thee, that thou hast brought so great a sin upon them?

modern.text: “What did this people do to you,” Moses asked Aaron, “that you have led them into so great a sin?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶֽל אַהֲרֹ֔ן מֶֽה עָשָׂ֥ה לְךָ֖ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֑ה כִּֽי הֵבֵ֥אתָ עָלָ֖יו חֲטָאָ֥ה גְדֹלָֽה

verses.restored: Aaron said, Let not anger of my lord burn. You know the people, that they are in harm.

familiar.text: And Aaron said, Let not the anger of my lord wax hot: thou knowest the people, that they are set on mischief.

modern.text: “Do not be enraged, my lord,” Aaron replied. “You yourself know that the people are intent on evil.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אַהֲרֹ֔ן אַל יִ֥חַר אַ֖ף אֲדֹנִ֑י אַתָּה֙ יָדַ֣עְתָּ אֶת הָעָ֔ם כִּ֥י בְרָ֖ע הֽוּא

verses.restored: They said to me, Make for us gods who will go before us; for this Moses, the man who brought us up from land of Egypt, we do not know what has become of him.

familiar.text: For they said unto me, Make us gods, which shall go before us: for as for this Moses, the man that brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we wot not what is become of him.

modern.text: They told me, ‘Make us gods who will go before us. As for this Moses who brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him!’

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמְרוּ לִ֔י עֲשֵׂה לָ֣נוּ אֱלֹהִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֵלְכ֖וּ לְפָנֵ֑ינוּ כִּי זֶ֣ה מֹשֶׁ֣ה הָאִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֤ר הֶֽעֱלָ֨נוּ֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם לֹ֥א יָדַ֖עְנוּ מֶה הָ֥יָה לֽוֹ

verses.restored: I said to them, Whoever has gold, tear it off. They gave it to me, and I threw it into fire, and this calf came out.

familiar.text: And I said unto them, Whosoever hath any gold, let them break it off. So they gave it me: then I cast it into the fire, and there came out this calf.

modern.text: So I said to them, ‘Whoever has gold, let him take it off,’ and they gave it to me. And when I threw it into the fire, out came this calf!”

original.text: וָאֹמַ֤ר לָהֶם֙ לְמִ֣י זָהָ֔ב הִתְפָּרָ֖קוּ וַיִּתְּנוּ לִ֑י וָאַשְׁלִכֵ֣הוּ בָאֵ֔שׁ וַיֵּצֵ֖א הָעֵ֥גֶל הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: Moses saw the people were let loose, for Aaron had let them loose, for whispering/shame among those rising against them.

familiar.text: And when Moses saw that the people were naked; (for Aaron had made them naked unto their shame among their enemies:)

modern.text: Moses saw that the people were out of control, for Aaron had let them run wild and become a laughingstock to their enemies.

original.text: וַיַּ֤רְא מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶת הָעָ֔ם כִּ֥י פָרֻ֖עַ ה֑וּא כִּֽי פְרָעֹ֣ה אַהֲרֹ֔ן לְשִׁמְצָ֖ה בְּקָמֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: Moses stood in gate of camp and said, Who is for YHWH? To me. All sons of Levi gathered to him.

familiar.text: Then Moses stood in the gate of the camp, and said, Who is on the LORD’s side? let him come unto me. And all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him.

modern.text: So Moses stood at the entrance to the camp and said, “Whoever is for the LORD, come to me.” And all the Levites gathered around him.

original.text: וַיַּעֲמֹ֤ד מֹשֶׁה֙ בְּשַׁ֣עַר הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מִ֥י לַיהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י וַיֵּאָסְפ֥וּ אֵלָ֖יו כָּל בְּנֵ֥י לֵוִֽי

verses.restored: He said to them, Thus says YHWH, Divine of Israel: Each man put sword on thigh; pass through and return from gate to gate in camp, and each kill brother, companion, and neighbor.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Put every man his sword by his side, and go in and out from gate to gate throughout the camp, and slay every man his brother, and every man his companion, and every man his neighbour.

modern.text: He told them, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘Each of you men is to fasten his sword to his side, go back and forth through the camp from gate to gate, and slay his brother, his friend, and his neighbor.’”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֗ם כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שִׂ֥ימוּ אִישׁ חַרְבּ֖וֹ עַל יְרֵכ֑וֹ עִבְר֨וּ וָשׁ֜וּבוּ מִשַּׁ֤עַר לָשַׁ֨עַר֙ בַּֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וְהִרְג֧וּ אִֽישׁ אֶת אָחִ֛יו וְאִ֥ישׁ אֶת רֵעֵ֖הוּ וְאִ֥ישׁ אֶת קְרֹבֽוֹ

verses.restored: Sons of Levi did according to word of Moses, and from the people fell that day about three thousand men.

familiar.text: And the children of Levi did according to the word of Moses: and there fell of the people that day about three thousand men.

modern.text: The Levites did as Moses commanded, and that day about three thousand of the people fell dead.

original.text: וַיַּֽעֲשׂ֥וּ בְנֵֽי לֵוִ֖י כִּדְבַ֣ר מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיִּפֹּ֤ל מִן הָעָם֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא כִּשְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת אַלְפֵ֖י אִֽישׁ

verses.restored: Moses said, Fill your hand today to YHWH, for each against his son and brother, so blessing may be given upon you today.

familiar.text: For Moses had said, Consecrate yourselves today to the LORD, even every man upon his son, and upon his brother; that he may bestow upon you a blessing this day.

modern.text: Afterward, Moses said, “Today you have been ordained for service to the LORD, since each man went against his son and his brother; so the LORD has bestowed a blessing on you this day.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֗ה מִלְא֨וּ יֶדְכֶ֤ם הַיּוֹם֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה כִּ֛י אִ֥ישׁ בִּבְנ֖וֹ וּבְאָחִ֑יו וְלָתֵ֧ת עֲלֵיכֶ֛ם הַיּ֖וֹם בְּרָכָֽה

verses.restored: It happened on next day Moses said to people, You sinned/misaligned a great sin/misalignment; and now I will go up to YHWH; perhaps I may make atonement for your sin/misalignment.

familiar.text: And it came to pass on the morrow, that Moses said unto the people, Ye have sinned a great sin: and now I will go up unto the LORD; peradventure I shall make an atonement for your sin.

modern.text: The next day Moses said to the people, “You have committed a great sin. Now I will go up to the LORD; perhaps I can make atonement for your sin.”

original.text: וַיְהִי֙ מִֽמָּחֳרָ֔ת וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל הָעָ֔ם אַתֶּ֥ם חֲטָאתֶ֖ם חֲטָאָ֣ה גְדֹלָ֑ה וְעַתָּה֙ אֶֽעֱלֶ֣ה אֶל יְהוָ֔ה אוּלַ֥י אֲכַפְּרָ֖ה בְּעַ֥ד חַטַּאתְכֶֽם

verses.restored: Moses returned to YHWH and said, Please, this people sinned/misaligned a great sin/misalignment and made for themselves gods of gold.

familiar.text: And Moses returned unto the LORD, and said, Oh, this people have sinned a great sin, and have made them gods of gold.

modern.text: So Moses returned to the LORD and said, “Oh, what a great sin these people have committed! They have made gods of gold for themselves.

original.text: וַיָּ֧שָׁב מֹשֶׁ֛ה אֶל יְהוָ֖ה וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אָ֣נָּ֗א חָטָ֞א הָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ חֲטָאָ֣ה גְדֹלָ֔ה וַיַּֽעֲשׂ֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם אֱלֹהֵ֥י זָהָֽב

verses.restored: And now, if you will lift/carry their sin/misalignment—but if not, blot me, please, from your scroll that you wrote.

familiar.text: Yet now, if thou wilt forgive their sin--; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written.

modern.text: Yet now, if You would only forgive their sin.... But if not, please blot me out of the book that You have written.”

original.text: וְעַתָּ֖ה אִם תִּשָּׂ֣א חַטָּאתָ֑ם וְאִם אַ֕יִן מְחֵ֣נִי נָ֔א מִֽסִּפְרְךָ֖ אֲשֶׁ֥ר כָּתָֽבְתָּ

verses.restored: YHWH said to Moses, Whoever sinned/misaligned against me, I will blot from my scroll.

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto Moses, Whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book.

modern.text: The LORD replied to Moses, “Whoever has sinned against Me, I will blot out of My book.

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל מֹשֶׁ֑ה מִ֚י אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָֽטָא לִ֔י אֶמְחֶ֖נּוּ מִסִּפְרִֽי

verses.restored: Now go, lead the people to what I spoke to you. Look, my messenger will go before you; and on day of my visitation, I will visit their sin/misalignment upon them.

familiar.text: Therefore now go, lead the people unto the place of which I have spoken unto thee: behold, mine Angel shall go before thee: nevertheless in the day when I visit I will visit their sin upon them.

modern.text: Now go, lead the people to the place I described. Behold, My angel shall go before you. But on the day I settle accounts, I will punish them for their sin.”

original.text: וְעַתָּ֞ה לֵ֣ךְ נְחֵ֣ה אֶת הָעָ֗ם אֶ֤ל אֲשֶׁר דִּבַּ֨רְתִּי֙ לָ֔ךְ הִנֵּ֥ה מַלְאָכִ֖י יֵלֵ֣ךְ לְפָנֶ֑יךָ וּבְי֣וֹם פָּקְדִ֔י וּפָקַדְתִּ֥י עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם חַטָּאתָֽם

verses.restored: YHWH struck the people because they made the calf, which Aaron made.

familiar.text: And the LORD plagued the people, because they made the calf, which Aaron made.

modern.text: And the LORD sent a plague on the people because of what they had done with the calf that Aaron had made.

original.text: וַיִּגֹּ֥ף יְהוָ֖ה אֶת הָעָ֑ם עַ֚ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשׂ֣וּ אֶת הָעֵ֔גֶל אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה אַהֲרֹֽן

translation_notes: Golden calf is covenant rupture and misattribution of liberation to a manufactured image.
Aaron's evasive account in v.24 should remain narratively ironic; do not soften his responsibility.
Moses intercession in vv.11-14 and vv.30-32 is central: he argues from YHWH's reputation, promise, and solidarity with the people.
Levite violence in vv.26-29 is severe and ethically dangerous; preserve source wording but flag against modern imitation or sanctification.
Broken tablets symbolize covenant fracture; later renewal must be read through intercession and YHWH's mercy.
safety_note: Do not use Exodus 32 to justify religious violence, purges, or coercive loyalty tests. The restored layer preserves the difficult ancient narrative; ethical application must center intercession, anti-idolatry, covenant rupture, accountability, and YHWH's later mercy proclamation.
